thread:
maria: customer reports 401 invalid_api_key after switching to our terraform provider v0.8. They say the key is injected via a k8s secret created by the provider.

customer: 'we call curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/engines/text:generate and get HTTP/1.1 401 {"error":{"type":"invalid_api_key","message":"Invalid API key"}}'

mike: thanks. do we have the terraform snippet they used? 

maria: pasted what they gave: 
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_secret" "redwood_key" {
  metadata { name = "redwood-key" }
  data = { api_key = var.redwood_api_key }
}
variable "redwood_api_key" { default = "sk_live_ABC123..." }
```
customer: they said they used the provider to sync a vault secret -> terraform var, then the k8s provider.

sarah: common culprit: extra newline/whitespace when the secret is read or passed through shell. can they show the actual bytes? suggest run: 
```bash
kubectl get secret redwood-key -o go-template='{{index .data "api_key"}}' | base64 -d | hexdump -C
```

devops: also check CI pipelines that do `echo $API_KEY > file` (this adds LF). `echo -n` avoids that.

maria: customer returned hexdump: 
```
00000000  73 6b 5f 6c 69 76 65 5f 41 42 43 31 32 33 0a     |sk_live_ABC123.|
0000000f
```

mike: confirmed trailing 0x0a (LF). that will cause signature mismatch -> 401.

support-bot: Created ticket CS-5321 and escalated to eng-oncall.

maria: mitigation for customer: rotate key from dashboard (new key won't have trailing LF) or update k8s secret to strip newline: 
```bash
# safe replacement
kubectl create secret generic redwood-key --from-literal=api_key="$(echo -n $API_KEY)" -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```

jordan: I'll add a defensive trim on our terraform provider when writing k8s secrets (and a test). Also add a note to the troubleshooting doc about echo vs echo -n, CI artifacts, and base64 pitfalls.

mike: I'll send repro steps + quick mitigation to the customer. closing loop once they confirm. :thumbsup:
